name: return_zero_stub
description: Library entry point that does nothing but return a zero result. It is reached through a pointer stored in the data area, not called directly by the code.

name: forward_library_call_and_check
description: Passes its second to fourth parameters to a library function call at vector offset minus 42 of the library base. It returns the fourth parameter when the call result equals it, and zero otherwise.

name: return_without_action
description: Empty library routine that returns at once without reading or writing any registers or memory.

name: forward_alternate_library_call

name: return_without_action

name: divide_32_by_32_bit
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor and returns the quotient and remainder together. Divisors above 65535 use a sixteen-step shift-and-subtract loop, while smaller divisors use two 16-bit divisions.

name: divide_with_sixteen_step_loop
description: Runs a sixteen-step shift-and-subtract division on a dividend and divisor held in registers. The quotient and remainder stay in those registers and the routine returns nothing.

name: multiply_32_bit_low_word
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values from the data registers using 16-bit partial products. The low 32 bits of the product fill the high half of the result, and the low half is the second operand with its 16-bit halves swapped.

name: invoke_stored_function_pointer
description: Calls the function whose address is stored at a fixed negative offset from a global base pointer. The facts identify that target as the Exec RawDoFmt formatting call.

name: store_byte_through_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of the first data register to the memory address held in an address register. Nothing is returned.

name: compute_string_checksum
description: Walks a null-terminated string and decrements the low 16 bits of a 32-bit accumulator once per character. It stops at the terminator or when that low half wraps around to all ones, and returns the bitwise complement of the accumulator.

name: find_char_in_string
description: Scans a null-terminated byte string for a given byte value and returns a pointer to its first occurrence. It returns zero if the terminator is reached first.

name: return_zero_entry
description: Library routine that returns a zero result immediately and makes no other calls or memory accesses.

name: copy_c_string
description: Copies a null-terminated byte string from the source pointer to the destination pointer, including the terminating zero byte.

name: append_c_string
description: Advances the destination pointer to the terminating zero of the existing string, then copies the source string there including its own terminator.

name: compare_bounded_strings
description: Compares two byte strings for up to a given count. It returns one at the first differing byte, and zero when the count runs out or both strings end together.

name: return_one_stub
description: Library entry point that does nothing but return a result of one.

name: scan_bounded_string_end
description: Walks a byte string for at most a given number of characters. If it reaches the zero terminator within that count it calls another library routine, and it returns without calling anything if the count runs out first.

name: call_companion_routine
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and then returns, so it works as a pass-through entry point.

name: copy_string_into_fixed_buffer
description: Copies a zero-terminated string into a buffer of a given length and stops early if the buffer fills. When the terminator is reached, it clears the rest of the buffer with zero bytes.

name: return_without_action
description: Empty library routine that returns at once without reading or writing any registers or memory.

name: initialize_self_linked_node
description: Sets the first longword of a block to point four bytes past its own start, clears the following word, and stores the block's own address in the third longword. The result is a small self-referencing node header.

name: validate_and_process_block
description: Returns one when its third argument is zero. Otherwise it calls a helper with the constant 20, and if that succeeds it makes two further calls and returns the result of a final helper that uses a field from the argument block.

name: walk_block_list_until_failure
description: Walks a linked list of records, running a helper on each record and then a second helper on the data it references, with a size scaled by four from a byte field. It returns one if every record passes and the list ends, and zero at the first failure.

name: return_one_entry
description: Library entry point that does nothing but return a result of one.

name: return_zero_entry
description: Library routine that returns a zero result immediately and makes no other calls or memory accesses.

name: create_block_with_link_field
description: When its fourth argument is nonzero, it obtains a 20-byte block from a helper, runs two more helper steps and stores one result at offset 10 of the block. It returns the block on success, minus one when a step fails, and zero when the fourth argument is zero.

name: return_minus_one_entry
description: Library entry point that returns minus one, with every bit of the result set, and does nothing else.

name: build_linked_block_chain
description: Repeatedly calls helpers to create blocks from a list of records, linking each new block to the previous one and to the next record. It returns minus one when a helper fails, and otherwise returns the first block built, or zero when no records are given.

name: walk_and_link_record_chain
description: Walks a chain of records through helper calls, linking each record to the previous one and checking every step. It returns the current record when the chain ends, and minus one if a helper call fails.

name: empty_entry_stub
description: Returns immediately in the decompiled body without doing any work. The listing also records one call that the pseudo-code does not show, so the routine is effectively empty.

name: return_minus_one_entry
description: Library entry point that returns minus one, with every bit of the result set, and does nothing else.

name: make_and_add_library_base
description: Creates a library structure through the Exec library-creation call, stores the global base pointer and the incoming argument into it, then registers it with the Exec add-library call. It returns minus one after registration, and zero when the structure could not be created.

name: increment_counter_clear_flag
description: Increments a 16-bit counter at offset 32 of the structure addressed by a base register, then clears bit five of the byte at offset 14.

name: decrement_counter_and_notify
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter at offset 32 of the addressed structure. When the counter reaches zero and the flag at bit five of the byte at offset 14 is set, it calls another routine and returns its result; otherwise it returns zero.

name: release_node_or_flag_pending
description: If the short at offset 8 is zero, it unlinks the structure from its doubly linked list, passes it to a library routine at offset minus 210 from the library base, and returns the longword at offset 38. Otherwise it sets bit five of the byte at offset 14 and returns zero.

name: unlink_node_and_release
description: Unlinks a node from its doubly linked list, calls a library routine at offset minus 210 from the library base, and returns the longword at offset 38 of the node.

name: return_zero_entry
description: Library routine that returns a zero result immediately and makes no other calls or memory accesses.

name: scan_text_into_space_buffer
description: Fills a 108-byte scratch area on the stack with space characters, then scans input text one character at a time. A hash mark and a space each lead to different helper calls, and the routine returns the value from the last helper once a counter goes negative.

name: return_low_word_of_d0
description: Returns the low 16-bit word of the first data register as a sign-extended integer, without making any other calls.

name: terminate_text_and_return_word
description: Calls a helper routine, then writes a zero byte just before the current text pointer to end a buffer. It returns the 16-bit value left in the second data register.

name: scan_field_until_separator
description: Scans text fields in step with a pattern pointer, calling helper routines for each field. It stops at a hash mark, at a space boundary, or when a count goes negative, and returns the last 16-bit result.

name: scan_fields_until_hash_mark
description: Steps through text fields with helper calls and returns the last 16-bit result when a hash mark is reached or a count goes negative. Otherwise it keeps scanning for the next space-separated boundary, then terminates the buffer on exit.

name: scan_escape_delimited_text
description: Reads text one character at a time, treating a backslash or backtick as a delimiter that triggers helper calls. The scan returns once a helper reports that it has finished.

name: advance_to_delimiter_pair
description: Advances through text to the next backslash or backtick, calls a helper at each delimiter, and returns when a helper reports completion through a flag.

name: return_without_action
description: Empty library routine that returns at once without reading or writing any registers or memory.

name: match_bracketed_tag_prefix
description: Skips forward to an opening square bracket in the text, then compares the characters that follow with a second string until a closing square bracket is reached or a character differs.

name: scan_backward_flagged_characters
description: Walks backward through text, testing each character against a flag bit in a character-class table. Flagged characters trigger a helper call, and the scan returns when the index goes negative or a helper reports completion.

name: return_without_action

name: scan_backward_matching_text
description: Walks backward through text while characters carry a flag in the character-class table, comparing the preceding characters with a second string. It returns at the first mismatch or when the index goes negative.

name: copy_text_until_equals
description: Reads text up to an equals sign, calling a helper for each flagged character and comparing the other characters with a second string. It returns at the equals sign or at the first mismatch.

name: match_text_until_equals
description: Reads text up to an equals sign, comparing unflagged characters with a second string and calling a helper for flagged ones. It returns at the first mismatch or at the equals sign.

name: copy_or_wrap_text_segment
description: Measures a text segment ending at a backslash or backtick. It copies the segment into the output and updates a status bit when it fits the remaining width; otherwise it backs up to the last break character and terminates the output there.

name: copy_known_segment_or_wrap
description: Copies a segment of known length into the output buffer unless the line width would be exceeded. In that case it backs up to the last break character, terminates the buffer there, and returns a computed position.

name: copy_counted_bytes_with_flag
description: Copies a counted run of bytes from the source to the output buffer. It then sets bit zero of a status byte when the last copied character is marked as a break, and clears that bit again if the next source byte is a backtick.

name: terminate_at_previous_break
description: Walks backward from the current output position to the nearest character marked as a break in the character-class table, then writes a zero byte there to end the line.

name: dispatch_special_character_handler
description: Searches a twelve-entry table of special characters for the byte in a data register, then calls the handler at the matching index of a jump table. The table holds the hash mark, asterisk, period, dollar sign, percent, ampersand, at-sign, caret, plus, colon, question mark and underscore.

name: insert_digit_four_at_position

name: allocate_info_structure_and_link

Otherwise it sets internal pointers to sub-blocks inside the new block, copies fixed word groups from a global template into them, sets up links between the sub-blocks, and returns one.

name: initialize_info_structure_pointers

name: acquire_library_handles_in_order

name: open_three_library_handles

name: open_two_library_handles

name: open_graphics_library_handle

name: lookup_field_via_pointer_chain

name: read_cached_or_chained_field
description: Returns a cached longword from the structure in an address register when it is set. Otherwise it follows a pointer chain to a second structure and returns a longword from there, or zero when the chain ends.

name: read_field_from_given_chain
description: Returns a longword from a structure reached through a pointer in an address register. It picks the first structure or a second pointer according to a type byte, and returns zero when the second pointer is null.

name: read_field_from_optional_pointer

name: build_disk_info_lookup

name: lookup_named_entry_with_fallback

name: create_info_entry_structure

name: create_entry_with_size_check
description: Stores a newly obtained block in an output field, verifies two lookups, then links sub-blocks and enforces a minimum size of 256 in one field. It allocates a block of that size, copies two fields, and returns one on success and zero otherwise.

name: finish_entry_setup_checked
description: Checks a lookup result and a status flag, then links sub-blocks and enforces a minimum size of 256 in one field. It allocates a block of that size, copies two fields, and returns one on success or zero when a step fails.

name: finish_entry_setup_after_probe
description: Checks a probe result, and when it is nonzero links sub-blocks, enforces a minimum size of 256 in one field, allocates a block of that size, copies two fields, and returns one. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: allocate_sized_entry_block
description: Links sub-blocks, enforces a minimum size of 256 in one field, and allocates a block of that size through a helper. It copies two fields when the allocation succeeds and returns whether it succeeded.

name: copy_struct_fields_from_source

name: setup_info_library_state

name: setup_entry_with_callback

name: setup_entry_with_reporter
description: Looks up a record and stores it in a target field, then copies fields and runs a sequence of helper calls. It reports code five when the first lookup fails, seven when the named lookup fails, one when a later check fails, and zero on success, all through an indirect callback.

name: setup_named_entry_callback

name: finish_entry_setup_callback

name: report_entry_status_callback

name: report_cleanup_status

name: run_cleanup_then_indirect_call

description: Calls a helper nine times with fixed index ranges and value pairs, passing the same first argument each time. It performs the same kind of table setup as its sibling routine, with different values.

name: build_info_list_entries
description: Chooses a base constant from a type byte in the state. It then makes either one fixed-argument helper call or an eleven-argument call, depending on whether a pointer chain ends, and finishes with a helper call that uses a field of the argument and a zero.

name: select_list_build_and_finish
description: Calls one of two helpers depending on whether a pointer chain ends, then calls a further helper with a field from the argument structure.

name: call_base_then_field_helper
description: Calls a library function at offset minus 222 from the library base with no arguments, then calls a helper with the field at offset 62 of the address-register structure.

name: build_node_list_from_table
description: Allocates a list head through a library call and links it to itself, then clears a status flag. It walks a zero-terminated table, allocating a node and a 128-byte block for each entry and linking the node in, and returns zero if any allocation fails.

name: relink_table_nodes
description: Updates the list head link and clears a status flag, then walks the zero-terminated table as its sibling does. It allocates and links a node for each entry, returns early if an allocation fails, and otherwise stores the first list element in the state.

name: link_table_entries_into_list
description: Walks a zero-terminated table, allocating a node for each entry, storing the table value in the node and linking it into the list. It returns zero when an allocation fails, and otherwise returns the result of the last link step.

name: append_table_values_to_list
description: Walks a table, storing each value into a list node and linking the node in. When the table ends it records the first element in the state and returns the last link result, or zero if a node cannot be obtained.

name: advance_list_cursor_and_notify
description: Checks whether the list cursor is at an end position. At an end it calls helpers with fields of the argument structure; otherwise it calls helpers with the current node's value, moves the cursor to the next node, and calls a helper with the argument.

name: step_list_cursor_forward
description: Calls a helper with the current node's value and a stored constant, calls a helper with no arguments, moves the cursor forward to the next node, and then calls another helper with no arguments.

name: reset_list_cursor_and_notify
description: Checks whether the list cursor is at an end position. At an end it calls helpers with fields of the argument structure; otherwise it calls helpers with the current node's value and resets the cursor to the first element of the list before calling a final helper.

name: follow_cursor_first_link
description: Calls a helper with the current node's value and a stored constant, calls a helper with no arguments, moves the cursor by following its first link, and then calls another helper with no arguments.

name: insert_node_at_cursor
description: Sets a status flag, and when the list is not at its end it calls two helpers for the current node. It then allocates a new node and a 128-byte payload, stores the payload pointer in the node, links the node in at the cursor, moves the cursor onto it, and calls a helper with the argument.

name: release_cursor_node_and_advance
description: Sets a status flag and, when the list is not at its end, calls two helpers for the current node. It then chooses a neighbouring link as the new cursor, calls a helper on the old cursor node, and calls a helper with the argument.

name: advance_cursor_with_wrap
description: Calls a helper with the current cursor node, then moves the cursor to the next link. When the list has reached its end, the cursor wraps to the first element, and a further helper is called with no arguments.

name: call_base_then_two_fields
description: Calls a helper with no arguments, then calls a helper with the field at offset 46 of the address-register structure, then a helper with the field at offset 62.

name: build_pointer_array_for_nodes
description: When a status flag in the state is set, it either clears the stored table pointer or counts the list nodes. For a non-empty list it allocates four bytes per node, stores the block address in the state, and fills it with a pointer for each node through helper calls, returning zero if an allocation fails.

name: build_pointer_array_for_list
description: Performs the same node counting, allocation and fill steps as its sibling routine, but without the status-flag test. It returns zero when an allocation fails.

name: clear_stored_table_pointer
description: Stores zero in the table pointer field of the state structure and returns one.

name: fill_node_pointer_array
description: Counts the nodes in the list, allocates a block of four bytes per node, and stores its address in the state. It then fills the block with a pointer for each node through helper calls, returning one on completion and zero if an allocation fails.

name: allocate_node_pointer_array
description: Counts the entries from a given pointer onward, allocates four bytes per entry, and stores the block in the state. It then fills the block with node pointers through helper calls, returning one on completion and zero if an allocation fails.

name: fill_node_array_from_list
description: Walks the list from its head, obtaining a slot value for each node through helper calls and storing node pointers in the array held in the state. It returns one when the walk completes and zero when an allocation fails.

name: fill_array_from_current_node
description: Walks the list starting at the current node, storing a helper-obtained pointer for each node in the array held in the state. It returns one when the walk reaches the end of the list and zero when an allocation fails.

name: fill_node_array_with_sizes
description: Walks the list nodes and stores a helper-obtained pointer for each node in the array held in the state, using a size taken from the previous node's value. It calls helpers for each node, returns one when the list is exhausted, and returns zero when an allocation fails.

name: draw_layout_for_mode
description: Switches on a mode byte in the state. For each of six modes it issues a fixed sequence of helper calls, passing pairs of coordinate-like values and text or field arguments, which lay out the screen elements for that mode.

name: return_without_action
description: Empty library routine that returns at once without reading or writing any registers or memory.

name: allocate_mode_buffers_and_draw
description: Allocates eight memory blocks of fixed sizes, two of them taken from the state, all with a fixed flag value, and returns zero if any block is missing. Otherwise it runs the helper sequence for the current mode and returns the result of the final helper, or the mode value for unlisted modes.

name: allocate_four_blocks_by_mode
description: Obtains four blocks through an indirect allocation call and stores the last one in a field of the state. It returns zero when a block is missing; otherwise it runs a number of helper calls chosen by the mode byte and returns the mode value.

name: run_helper_sequence_by_mode
description: Runs a number of helper calls chosen by the mode byte in the state: two for mode one, three for modes two and five, four for mode three, and five for mode four. Other modes make no calls.

name: return_without_action
description: Empty library routine that returns at once without reading or writing any registers or memory.

name: clear_or_copy_status_probe
description: Clears a status longword when a state field is zero, or copies a global text into it otherwise. It then calls a helper with the argument, a global pointer and minus one, and returns zero when that call returns minus one, otherwise its result.

name: probe_after_copy_status
description: Copies a state field into a global pointer target through a helper, then calls a second helper. It returns zero when that result is minus one, and otherwise returns the result.

name: set_probe_fields_and_check
description: When the mode byte is not four, it writes four 16-bit values into a field at offset six of four structures. It then calls a helper on each structure with minus one as a second argument, and returns one when none of the four calls returns minus one, otherwise zero.

name: check_three_probes_for_success
description: Calls an indirect routine three times with no arguments. It returns zero if any call returns minus one, and one when all three succeed.

name: check_two_probes_for_success
description: Calls an indirect routine twice with no arguments. It returns zero if either call returns minus one, and one when both succeed.

name: check_single_probe_result
description: Calls an indirect routine with no arguments and returns whether its result is not minus one.

name: return_one_entry
description: Library routine that returns a result of one without any other work.

name: service_port_items_or_wait
description: Loops over a port-like structure, passing each item fetched from the state to a helper with the second argument and returning zero on failure. When no item is ready it waits on a signal mask built from a bit number stored in the structure, using a library call at offset minus 318 and the Exec permit call.

name: return_zero_entry
description: Library routine that returns a zero result immediately and makes no other calls or memory accesses.

name: dispatch_by_flag_value
description: Reads a flag value from the argument's structure. The value four calls a helper on a field and then a final helper that returns one; the value 64 returns the result of a helper call; the value 512 calls a helper and returns zero; other values call the final helper and return one.

name: dispatch_flag_and_report
description: Calls one helper when the flag value is 64, returning its result. For other values it calls a helper and returns one unless the flag is 512, in which case it returns zero.

name: report_flag_value_status
description: Calls one helper when the flag value is 512 and another helper otherwise, then returns whether the flag is not 512.

name: call_companion_routine
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and then returns, so it works as a pass-through entry point.
